_comment: Ground truth from the Scala reference stack (sigma-state 6.0.2 + ergo-core 6.0.2)
for getVar / getReg type-mismatch semantics -- an accept-invalid fork vector.
PRESENT-BUT-WRONG-TYPE. An absent slot returns None. A present slot whose stored
RType does not match the requested one falls to the `case _` arm and THROWS
InvalidType -- it does NOT return None. An implementation that returns None for a
present-but-mistyped var SATISFIES scripts the reference node fails, e.g.
sigmaProp(getVar[Long](1).isDefined == false) over an extension binding var 1 to an Int.
The box-register analogue behaves identically (Cannot getReg[Long](4)).
The v6 SContext.getVarFromInput does NOT: its implementation
(CContext.scala:76-82) pattern-matches the RType and falls through to
`case _ => None`, so a mismatch there is None, not a throw.
